chapter: Europe and the Black and Blue years
title: Hotel treatment in Sweden and keeping some privacy
summary: Hosts took her to meals and tipped for her; she tipped her maid and clerks. She says she gets privacy by telling people not to call before a certain time, but otherwise just grins and bears it.

But I didn't cook. They would come and get me, take me to breakfast. I'd say, I don't want no breakfast. You can take me for dinner later. Then after work they'd take me somewhere for supper. And I said, shucks . . . I never had anything like this. And they did all the tipping and everything. But when I got ready to leave I tipped my maid and I tipped my little clerks downstairs because they were all so nice to me.
Helen, don't you find, isn't it a little hard traveling and working like that? I mean, you don't get very much privacy, do you? You know, you're almost always on exhibition.
That's right. But look, I get some privacy because I tell them, don't call be before such and such a time.
Well, what about times, especially lately, you know, when you haven't felt well, I mean, like we all do, there are times we didn't have to talk to anybody.
